Dr. Brian Mazjanis, Assistant Superintendent for Finance gave an overview of the project which began 
back in 2023.  This is a project that allows us to make our schools more energy efficient at 0 cost to our 
budget over the life of the loan. 
 
Phase 1 was LED lighting, some HVAC work and saving heating costs by using a building envelope.  
 
Phase 2 was adding solar panels to some of our schools to run those schools and potentially generate 
electricity that we can sell back to the electric company.  Some schools now have a credit; while this does 
not produce actual monies, it will give us credit when we move into the colder, darker months of the year.

RELATIONS WITH LAW ENFORCEMENT PERSONNEL: LIMITATIONS ON AUTHORITY TO 
CONSENT FOR  ENTRY OR TO REVIEW RECORDS IN SCHOOLS 
 
 
The intent of the policy is to ensure that the Westbrook School Department schools and educational 
programs remain safe and accessible to all students and staff regardless of immigration status by limiting, 
to the fullest extent possible, consistent with state and federal law, voluntary consent for entry into 
nonpublic areas of the facility by law enforcement officers for immigration enforcement purposes, and 
limiting consent to disclosure of protected records held by the school to law enforcement officers for 
immigration enforcement purposes. 
 
In the context of this policy, “voluntary consent” means that no school district employee, acting on their 
own initiative, may voluntarily consent or acquiesce to the request of a federal law enforcement officer to 
enter a nonpublic space within the school or allow access to, or inspection of, education records 
maintained by the school for the purpose of enforcing immigration laws. Access to nonpublic spaces or 
education records will only be provided when legally required at the direction of the Superintendent or 
designee after consultation with Westbrook School Department’s attorney, if appropriate.  
 
The school principal/designated administrator will ensure that all staff persons who may interact with law 
enforcement officers are informed of this policy. All staff persons should have the name, title, and contact 
information of the administrator who has been designated to advise them in implementing this policy.   
 
I. Definitions 
 
A. “Education record” has the same meaning as in the federal Family Educational Rights and 
Privacy Act of 1974 (FERPA), 20 United States Code, Section 1232g(a)(4), and its implementing 
regulations. 
 
B. “Law enforcement officer” means a person who by virtue of public employment is vested by law 
with a duty to maintain public order, to prosecute offenders, to make arrests for crimes, whether 
that duty extends to all crimes or is limited to specific crimes, or to perform probation functions, or 
who is an adult probation supervisor. 
 
“Law enforcement officer” includes the following federal officers who are authorized to carry 
firearms in the performance of their duties as federal law enforcement employees or officers:  
• Special Agents: A federal officer who is a special agent of the United States Secret 
Service of the Department of Homeland Security; and 
 
 
• Immigration, Customs, or Border Security: A federal officer of an agency within the 
Department of Homeland Security that has administrative and enforcement jurisdiction 
over immigration, customs, or border security matters. This may include, for example, a 
federal officer within the United States Customs and Border Protection, United States 
Immigration and Customs Enforcement, or United States Citizenship and Immigration 
Services. 
 
C. “Nonpublic area” means an area of a building or facility that the public is not free to enter or 
access and includes a restricted access area within a building or facility that is otherwise 
predominately open to the public. “Nonpublic area” also includes all areas within a building or 
facility during any time that the building or facility is closed for operation. 
 
II. Responding to Requests for Entry and Access to Records Maintained by the School

A. Entry Into Nonpublic Areas 
 
A person acting on behalf of a public school may not voluntarily permit a law enforcement officer 
to enter a nonpublic area of the school for immigration enforcement purposes. 
 
If a law enforcement officer presents at the school and seeks to gain entry to nonpublic areas, the 
staff person shall ask the law enforcement officer to identify their purpose for accessing nonpublic 
areas.  
 
If the law enforcement officer indicates an immigration enforcement purpose, the staff person 
shall ask the law enforcement officer to produce a court-issued warrant or any other documents 
the officer contends authorize access to  nonpublic areas of the school.  
 
The staff person shall inform the officer of the requirement to consult with a designated 
administrator to review the warrant or other legal documents prior to permitting access to any 
nonpublic areas of the school. 
 
The staff person shall direct the officer to wait in a designated area of the school (e.g., principal’s 
office or conference room) while the principal/designated administrator reviews the documents.  
 
The principal/designated administrator will notify the Superintendent of the presence of the 
federal law enforcement official(s) and reason for the request.  
 
The principal/designated administrator will review the documents presented and consult with legal 
counsel, as necessary, before giving direction to the staff person as to how to respond.  
 
If the law enforcement officer insists on accessing nonpublic areas without a court-ordered 
warrant or other valid order authorizing access under federal or state law, or before the 
principal/designated administrator has reviewed the documents presented and provided direction 
to staff, the officer should be informed that the school objects to the officer’s entry into the 
nonpublic areas. The staff should immediately inform the principal/designated administrator but 
should not attempt to physically interfere with the officer or obstruct the officer’s entry into the 
nonpublic areas. The designated administrator will contact the Superintendent, who will contact 
the district’s legal counsel and/or the Westbrook Police Department 
 
B. Access to Education Records 
 
A person acting on behalf of a Westbrook School Department may not voluntarily permit a law 
enforcement officer to access education records for immigration enforcement purposes.  
 
The principal/designated administrator school shall ensure that all staff persons who have access 
to education records are informed of this policy, and that those persons have the name, title, and 
contact information of an administrator who has been designated to advise them in implementing 
this policy. 
 
If a law enforcement officer seeks access to education records, the staff person shall ask the law 
enforcement officer to identify their purpose for accessing education records.  
 
If the law enforcement officer indicates an immigration enforcement purpose, the staff person 
shall ask the law enforcement officer to produce a court-issued warrant or any other documents 
the officer contends authorize access under federal or state law. 
 
The staff person shall inform the officer of the need to consult with the principal/designated 
administrator to review the warrant or other legal documents prior to allowing access to any 
nonpublic areas of the school for review or inspection of records.

III. Mandatory Compliance Activities 
 
If required by federal law to permit the inspection of educational records or to conduct interviews 
regarding the eligibility of noncitizens to work in the United States or to attend school in the United States:  
 
 
1. The school shall designate a nonpublic area within the school institution where law enforcement 
officers may conduct these inspections and interviews; and 
 
 
2. The school may permit law enforcement officers to access a specific location to verify eligibility for 
employment or school attendance if applicable federal law requires that law enforcement officers 
be provided access to that specific location within the school when conducting these inspections 
and interviews. 
 
IV.  Policy Review 
 
In compliance with Maine law, 5 MRSA §200-O(2), the Board will review and amend this policy, as

policies and guidance applicable to Maine’s public schools.
